utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everybody. Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-04-83-I, the Prosecutor against Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. May I have the appearances.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. The Prosecution is represented by trial attorney Daryl Mundis and my name is Hildegard Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. Representing General Delic this morning, Stephane Bourgon, lawyer from Montreal, Canada, and I am accompanied this morning, Your Honour, by Mr. Asim Crnalic and Mrs. Vedrana Residovic. As indicated yesterday, I wish to be accompanied by Mr. Crnalic and Ms. Residovic, and I am ready to make the necessary application in this regard at your convenience, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So as long as you will represent the Defence and the accused today and Mr. Crnalic is here as a sort of assistant to you, I don't see any problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour. If I may just provide you with a little background as to why Mr. Crnalic is here this morning. I believe that it is important to make this on the record and I would like to do this in closed session, with your permission, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, can you hear the proceedings in a language that you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you could rise and identify yourself with your full name and date of birth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, my name is Rasim Delic. I was born on 4th February, 1949, at Celic in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which is in Lopare municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, prior to the war this was Lopare municipality; now it is Celic municipality. When I was born there it was Celic municipality. Lopare is now in Republika Srpska and Celic is in the Federation; that's why it's the Celic municipality now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for the clarification. You may sit now, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: First of all, I'd like to apologise to everybody here for holding a hearing at this early time of the day, in particular given the heavy snow which had fallen yesterday; however, I was told that since all the courtrooms are fully booked for the whole week with ongoing trials, this was the only option for having an initial appearance hearing. This proceeding is the initial appearance of Mr. Rasim Delic pursuant to Rule 62 of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence of the International Tribunal. The indictment against the accused was reviewed and confirmed by a permanent Judge of this Tribunal on 16th of February, 2005, and Mr. Delic was transferred to The Hague on 28th of February. This case was assigned to Trial Chamber III by the order of the President of the Tribunal, and I was assigned as the Pre-Trial Judge by the Chamber. I am Judge Kwon. The first thing I have to do is to make certain that accused understands the indictment against him. Mr. Bourgon, has your client received the client in his own language?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I can confirm this morning that I have met with General Delic on two occasions; that General Delic has received a copy of the indictment in his language; that General Delic understands the nature of the charges laid against him; and I have also explained to General Delic the contents of the indictment as well as the procedure which will be followed this morning and subsequently. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. The next step is then -- well, before that, it is the right of the accused to have the indictment read out in full in a language he understands. Mr. Bourgon, does your client wish to have the indictment read out in full?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. After discussing the matter with General Delic, he waives his right to have the indictment read. I take this opportunity, Your Honour, to clarify one issue which maybe was not put on the record up until now, which is the fact that General Delic surrendered at the first -- to the first opportunity, as soon as he was informed of the indictment ever existing. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Then the next step is then entry of a plea to the charges of the indictment. The accused may enter a plea within 30 days of the initial appearance, but he may enter a plea at the time of initial appearance if he so wishes. Mr. Bourgon, does your client wish to plead today or do it later?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have discussed the matter with General Delic and he is ready to enter a plea at this time on the four charges included in the indictment. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then, Mr. Delic, if you could rise and please plead to each count of the indictment, which I will put to you. In entering a plea, please confine your answer to either guilty or not guilty. Count 1 of the indictment charges you in relation to the events at Maline or Bikosi in 1993 and at Manjaca camp in 1995 with murder as a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Articles 3(1)(A) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead to this count?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Count 2 charges you in relation to the same events with cruel treatment as a violation of the laws and customs of war, punishable under Article 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Articles 3(1)(A) of the Geneva Conventions. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Count 3 charges you in relation to what happened to three women in Kamenica camp in September 1995 with rape as a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal. How do you plead?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And finally, Count 4 charges you in relation to the same matter with cruel treatment as a violation of the laws or customs of war, punishable under Article 3 and 7(3) of the Statute of the Tribunal and recognised by Articles 3(1)(A) of the Geneva Conventions. How do you plead, Mr. Delic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, not guilty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. You may now sit down. I would like to ask the registrar to note that Mr. Delic has pleaded not guilty to all the counts of the indictment. Mrs. Uertz-Retzlaff, I must remind the Prosecution now of its duty pursuant to Rule 66(A)(1) to make available within 30 days from now to the Defence all the supporting material which accompanied the indictment when confirmation was sought as well as prior statements obtained by the Prosecution from the accused in a language which the accused understands. Is there any problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, there's no problem. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then let me now turn to the Defence. I am hereby informing the Defence that pursuant to Rule 72(A) it will have a 30-day period for filing any preliminary motions once it has received all the supporting materials in accordance with Rule 66(A)(i). You understand that?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, the Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. The Defence understands and accepts its duties and responsibilities pursuant to the Rules. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I will have a Status Conference within approximately four months' time from now. I will let the parties be informed in due course. In the meantime, pursuant to Rule 65 ter, the Pre-Trial Judge may be assisted in the performance of his duties by the Senior Legal Officer of the Chamber. In this regard, I believe the Senior Legal Officer will schedule a meeting with the parties after the time period for the Rule 66(A)(i) disclosure and before the date of the next Status Conference in due course in due manner. I think I've dealt with all the items I've noted down for today's agenda. Is there anything the parties wish to raise now? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. As a preliminary matter, Your Honour, I would like to confirm that General Delic since his arrival at the United Nations Detention Unit has been treated well and that he has no complaint in this regard. However, there is one issue I wish to raise on behalf of General Delic concerning his right to be represented by counsel of his choice before the International Tribunal, and to this end I would like to move into closed session and make some observations, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For the purpose of putting it on record?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is there anything for the Prosecution to raise at this moment?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Delic, apart from what is said by Mr. Bourgon, is there anything you would like to raise now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as Mr. Bourgon has already stated, I would like be assigned a permanent counsel as soon as possible. I have stated my opinion in that regard; I believe there is no conflict of interest here. In the interest of justice, I believe this problem should be solved as soon as possible. As for the rest, I have been treated well and I have nothing to comment upon in that sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is the problem fixed? Yes, its seems to be okay. Yes, please go on, Mr. Delic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Delic. I think -- or I believe the registrar and the whole Tribunal will do its best and make sure that there will be no -- any disadvantage on the part of the accused in relation to the counsel issue. The hearing is now adjourned.
